Are you looking for a fulfilling career that provides you the opportunity to work on a variety of projects across the state? We are looking for an Environmental Scientist to join our diverse, dynamic, and multi-disciplinary team in the Financial Assistance Branch. **Company Description**

**Work with Us. Change the World.**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**

AECOM is seeking a GIS Specialist to make complex field information useful for federal facility assessment and hurricane recovery work in Kauai, Hawaii. Engineering teams may inspect damaged roofs and buildings, assess utilities and access routes, and define immediate repairs across multiple locations. You will turn inspection findings, photos, asset records, and field coordinates into maps and spatial data that show where damage occurred and what work remains. Your products will support the initial assessment report, help teams plan access and repair priorities, and give project leaders a clearer picture as conditions change.

**This role will require an onsite presence in Kauai, Hawaii and is eligible for per diem related expenses when appropriate.**

Key Responsibilities

* Create and maintain GIS maps, geodatabases, dashboards, and spatial datasets for facilities and infrastructure.
* Integrate field survey information, photographs, inspection findings, and asset records into consistent GIS products.
* Support mobile data collection and establish quality control procedures for field updates.
* Prepare maps and exhibits for assessment reports, repair plans, site access, and construction coordination.
* Analyze spatial data to identify affected facilities, utility corridors, access routes, and repair priorities.
* Coordinate with engineers, construction managers, and field teams to resolve data gaps and maintain accurate records.

  
**Qualifications**

**Minimum Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in geography, geographic information systems, geospatial science, engineering, or a related field and 4+ years of GIS mapping and spatial data management for infrastructure, facilities, or construction projects or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
* A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
* Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 8+ years of GIS mapping and spatial data management for infrastructure, facilities, or construction projects.
* Experience with Esri ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, Field Maps, or Survey123.
* Experience with federal facility mapping, utility systems, or post event damage assessments.

  
**Additional Information**

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. ***To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.***

**About AECOM**

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

**What makes AECOM a great place to work**

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

**Title-** Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Coordinator

**Classification-** Construction Project Coordinator 4

**Job Status-** Full-Time - Permanent  
**WDFW Program-** Capital Asset ManagementProgram (CAMP)  
**Duty Station-** Olympia, Washington – Thurston County

  
  

Learn more about being a member of **Team WDFW**!

  
  
  
  

*Photo Caption: Newman Lake Crane Work – Photo Credit: WDFW*

  

**With your expertise in construction project management, lead and support a team of construction project professionals while guiding the successful delivery of complex and high-priority projects.**

  

**Serve as the department’s** **Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) coordinator and provide project leadership, technical guidance, and oversight for major construction projects from planning through completion.**

  

**What to Expect:**

  
  

Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, the Construction Project Supervisor will,

  

**Perform Supervision and Mentoring:**

* Supervise and mentor technical and professional level staff to support an effective, motivated team.
* Manage personnel issues relating to staff conflicts, absenteeism, performance issues in a positive manner for the purpose of ensuring the efficient and effective functioning of the work unit.
* Participate in team meetings, communicate status of ongoing projects and/or job tasks, and coordinate work schedule with the team.
* Plan and maintain work systems, procedures, and policies that enable and encourage the optimum performance of its people and other resources within the unit.
  

  

**Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Coordinator:**

* Serve as the primary point-of-contact with FEMA and the Emergency Management Division (EMD) of Washington Military Department providing professional level written and verbal communications.
* Disseminate key FEMA Public Assistance Program information to Department staff and provide guidance on qualified events, required processes, procedures, and necessary steps to document damages and request FEMA funding in consultation with EMD.
* Organize, schedule, and facilitate on-site meetings with EMD, FEMA, and department staff to review damages and discuss Public Assistance project categories.

**Role** - The Lead Operations Geologist provides technical and organizational leadership across pre-drill planning, real-time drilling operations, and post-well evaluation. The successful candidate will manage geosteering personnel and contractors, establish clear operating standards, and ensure that geologic interpretations are translated into timely, practical recommendations for drilling operations.

The main responsibilities will be to integrate subsurface interpretation, well planning, drilling data, and operational constraints. The Lead Operations Geologist will work closely with asset geologists, drilling engineers, drill-site personnel, reservoir engineering, completions, land, regulatory, and other subsurface disciplines to support safe, efficient, and technically sound well delivery.

**Responsibilities**

**Geosteering Leadership**

* Lead daily geosteering activities, staffing, coverage, priorities, and escalation protocols.
* Review real-time interpretations, landing recommendations, directional targets, and operational communications.
* Provide technical guidance during uncertain or rapidly changing drilling conditions.
* Mentor personnel and improve team capabilities, workflows, reporting, and quality control.
* Ensure recommendations are technically supported, clearly communicated, and properly documented.

**Pre-Drill Geologic Planning**

* Manage geologic deliverables required to prepare wells and pads for drilling.
* Develop geologic prognosis packages, including formation tops, targets, landing strategies, structural interpretations, offset correlations, risks, and uncertainties.
* Integrate logs, seismic, core, mudlogs, geochemistry, petrophysics, production, and offset-well data.
* Coordinate geologic inputs for directional plans, bottom-hole locations, target lines, and landing points.
* Support pilot-hole, logging, coring, mudlogging, and sampling programs.

**Real-Time Operations Support**

* Provide operational geology oversight from spud through total depth, with particular focus on curve and lateral execution.
* Integrate real-time drilling parameters, directional surveys, logging-while-drilling data, mudlogs, gas data, cuttings descriptions, and offset-well information.
* Review proposed directional targets and significant interpretation changes before they are communicated to the drilling team.
* Maintain close communication with drill-site managers, drilling engineers, asset geologists, mudloggers, geosteerers, and other operational personnel.

* Lead post-well reviews and finalize geosteering interpretations.
* Track performance measures related to placement, interpretation quality, and operational efficiency.
* Maintain standardized procedures, templates, technical documentation, and data-quality practices.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Serve as the primary interface between geosteering, geoscience, drilling, and operations.
* Balance reservoir objectives with directional constraints, operational risk, and drilling efficiency.
* Communicate interpretations, uncertainties, recommendations, and business implications to technical and non-technical audiences.
* Support broader development, appraisal, and operational initiatives as needed.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Geoscience, Geophysics, or a related discipline.
* 10 or more years of oil and gas geoscience experience, including operations geology and geosteering.
* Experience supporting unconventional horizontal-well development.

**Skills & Attributes**

* Strong knowledge of pre-drill planning, landing strategy, well correlation, structural interpretation, and real-time well placement.
* Ability to integrate geologic, petrophysical, directional, and drilling data in real time.
* Experience leading or mentoring geosteering personnel or other technical professionals.
* Advanced proficiency with geosteering and subsurface interpretation software.
* Strong communication, organizational, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to manage multiple active wells and make timely recommendations with incomplete or evolving information.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Geology, Geoscience, Geophysics, or a related discipline.
* Powder River Basin, Rockies, or comparable multi-zone unconventional experience.
* Experience utilizing data visualization and analytics platforms (Spotfire, Power BI, Python, SQL, or similar) to evaluate drilling, geosteering, completion, and production datasets
* Demonstrated ability to identify trends, develop performance metrics, and translate large subsurface datasets into actionable recommendations that improve well placement, drilling execution, and development outcomes
* Advanced experience with StarSteer and multi-well geosteering workflows.
* Experience with GeoGraphix, Spotfire, or similar platforms.
* Experience developing operations geology procedures and quality-control workflows.
* Experience planning and evaluating logging, coring, mudlogging, and geochemical programs.
* Demonstrated record of improving team capability, or well-delivery performance.

**Work with Us. Change the World.**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**

AECOM is seeking a GIS Specialist to make complex field information useful for federal facility assessment and hurricane recovery work in Kauai, Hawaii. Engineering teams may inspect damaged roofs and buildings, assess utilities and access routes, and define immediate repairs across multiple locations. You will turn inspection findings, photos, asset records, and field coordinates into maps and spatial data that show where damage occurred and what work remains. Your products will support the initial assessment report, help teams plan access and repair priorities, and give project leaders a clearer picture as conditions change.

**This role will require an onsite presence in Kauai, Hawaii and is eligible for per diem related expenses when appropriate.**

Key Responsibilities

* Create and maintain GIS maps, geodatabases, dashboards, and spatial datasets for facilities and infrastructure.
* Integrate field survey information, photographs, inspection findings, and asset records into consistent GIS products.
* Support mobile data collection and establish quality control procedures for field updates.
* Prepare maps and exhibits for assessment reports, repair plans, site access, and construction coordination.
* Analyze spatial data to identify affected facilities, utility corridors, access routes, and repair priorities.
* Coordinate with engineers, construction managers, and field teams to resolve data gaps and maintain accurate records.

  
**Qualifications**

**Minimum Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in geography, geographic information systems, geospatial science, engineering, or a related field and 4+ years of GIS mapping and spatial data management for infrastructure, facilities, or construction projects or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
* A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
* Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 8+ years of GIS mapping and spatial data management for infrastructure, facilities, or construction projects.
* Experience with Esri ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, Field Maps, or Survey123.
* Experience with federal facility mapping, utility systems, or post event damage assessments.

AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Description:

**Role** - The Lead Operations Geologist provides technical and organizational leadership across pre-drill planning, real-time drilling operations, and post-well evaluation. The successful candidate will manage geosteering personnel and contractors, establish clear operating standards, and ensure that geologic interpretations are translated into timely, practical recommendations for drilling operations.

The main responsibilities will be to integrate subsurface interpretation, well planning, drilling data, and operational constraints. The Lead Operations Geologist will work closely with asset geologists, drilling engineers, drill-site personnel, reservoir engineering, completions, land, regulatory, and other subsurface disciplines to support safe, efficient, and technically sound well delivery.

**Responsibilities**

**Geosteering Leadership**

* Lead daily geosteering activities, staffing, coverage, priorities, and escalation protocols.
* Review real-time interpretations, landing recommendations, directional targets, and operational communications.
* Provide technical guidance during uncertain or rapidly changing drilling conditions.
* Mentor personnel and improve team capabilities, workflows, reporting, and quality control.
* Ensure recommendations are technically supported, clearly communicated, and properly documented.

**Pre-Drill Geologic Planning**

* Manage geologic deliverables required to prepare wells and pads for drilling.
* Develop geologic prognosis packages, including formation tops, targets, landing strategies, structural interpretations, offset correlations, risks, and uncertainties.
* Integrate logs, seismic, core, mudlogs, geochemistry, petrophysics, production, and offset-well data.
* Coordinate geologic inputs for directional plans, bottom-hole locations, target lines, and landing points.
* Support pilot-hole, logging, coring, mudlogging, and sampling programs.

**Real-Time Operations Support**

* Provide operational geology oversight from spud through total depth, with particular focus on curve and lateral execution.
* Integrate real-time drilling parameters, directional surveys, logging-while-drilling data, mudlogs, gas data, cuttings descriptions, and offset-well information.
* Review proposed directional targets and significant interpretation changes before they are communicated to the drilling team.
* Maintain close communication with drill-site managers, drilling engineers, asset geologists, mudloggers, geosteerers, and other operational personnel.

**Post-Well Evaluation and Continuous Improvement**

* Lead post-well reviews and finalize geosteering interpretations.
* Track performance measures related to placement, interpretation quality, and operational efficiency.
* Maintain standardized procedures, templates, technical documentation, and data-quality practices.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Serve as the primary interface between geosteering, geoscience, drilling, and operations.
* Balance reservoir objectives with directional constraints, operational risk, and drilling efficiency.
* Communicate interpretations, uncertainties, recommendations, and business implications to technical and non-technical audiences.
* Support broader development, appraisal, and operational initiatives as needed.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Geoscience, Geophysics, or a related discipline.
* 10 or more years of oil and gas geoscience experience, including operations geology and geosteering.
* Experience supporting unconventional horizontal-well development.

* Strong knowledge of pre-drill planning, landing strategy, well correlation, structural interpretation, and real-time well placement.
* Ability to integrate geologic, petrophysical, directional, and drilling data in real time.
* Experience leading or mentoring geosteering personnel or other technical professionals.
* Advanced proficiency with geosteering and subsurface interpretation software.
* Strong communication, organizational, and decision-making skills.
